# Balanced crypto-cluster split — baseline vs new (Strategy Logic V2)

*Generated by `scripts/eval_cluster_mix.py` · data through **2026-10-10** · Balanced profile · walk-forward gated replay, 3 optimiser seeds (7, 11, 23; 7 = production) · cells are **total return / max drawdown / Sharpe**.*

## Question

The BTC parent cluster — BTC · MSTR · MSTU · ETH — trades **one** signal (the four sleeves enter and exit together on ~98 % of days), so how the cluster's weight is *divided* is purely a vehicle-mix choice, not a timing one. The V2 allocator let the optimiser anchors × entry-priority tilt decide the split — erratically (one day 29 % in BTC, another 25 % in ETH, the weakest sleeve). Does a **fixed, ordered split** do better, without more drawdown?

## The rule

`overall_core.CLUSTER_MIX_BALANCED` (V2 only, **Balanced profile only**): the cluster is sized exactly as before (anchor × priority tilt, water-filled to the per-sleeve caps, bound by the 30 % parent-cluster cap), then its combined weight is **divided**: **MSTR 45 %** · **MSTU 30 %** · **BTC 20 %** · **ETH 5 %**. Shares are renormalised over the members actually funded and every member stays inside its per-sleeve cap (at a full 30 % cluster: MSTR 13.5 % ≤ 18 %, MSTU 9 % ≤ 10 %, BTC 6 %, ETH 1.5 %). The split is applied to the **tilt target before the adds-only pin**: fresh entries are sized at the split, held names are never re-split or trimmed. V1, Growth and Aggressive are unchanged.

### How the split was chosen

A post-hoc study re-divided the *unchanged* V2 Balanced cluster weights over an ordered grid (MSTR ≥ MSTU ≥ BTC ≥ ETH, 5 % steps, all four names, per-sleeve caps respected) and ranked them by selection-window return with max drawdown no more than 1 pt worse than V2. The top mix was 50 / 30 / 15 / 5 (+328 %); the originally proposed 45 / 35 / 15 / 5 would put MSTU at 10.5 % of the book, above Balanced's 10 % 2× cap, so the cap-compliant neighbour **45 / 30 / 20 / 5** (+325 %, same hold-out) was adopted — all 28 Balanced grid mixes beat V2 in both windows, so the choice sits on a plateau, not a spike. Growth and Aggressive showed no hold-out edge (3 of 41 and 0 of 41 mixes beat V2 in both windows, within the drawdown limit), so they keep the tilt split. A MSTU-only cluster earned more return still, but by concentrating 2× leverage in one name (deeper Growth drawdown, thin hold-out edge) — not adopted.

Realised shares drift from 45/30/20/5 only on the days the four sleeves do not enter/exit together (e.g. BTC alone held after its siblings exit) and while adds-only pins a previously-sized name.

## No-degradation gate

For every window × cost × (3-seed mean, production seed): new Sharpe ≥ baseline, new return no more than 0.5 pt below baseline, new max drawdown no more than 0.5 pt deeper. (The return tolerance was added after the first run showed a 0.1-pt shortfall — hold-out, production seed, +183.3 % vs +183.4 % — with better Sharpe and drawdown; an exactly-zero tolerance fails on rounding.)

**PASS** — no window, cost level or seed view degrades.

## Caveats

* The crypto sleeves only exist from 2024-03 and the cluster is held on ~10 % of days (about 8–10 trades), so the edge is small in absolute terms and sits inside the optimiser-seed spread on the full window; the *direction* is consistent (new ≥ baseline on every seed and window) but not statistically strong. The hold-out is not fully clean: the post-hoc grid study had seen full-sample results.
* MSTU's history before 2024-09 is the committed OLS-synthetic series.
* Costs are a flat 5 bp on target-weight changes (no spread widening, no drift between rebalances).
* Live effect is nil until a crypto signal fires: the published book holds no crypto sleeve today; the next BTC-cluster entry is sized at the split.
